function rMultiplesInsights(f: AnalyticsFacts): Insight[] {
  const out: Insight[] = [];
  const total = sum(f.rHistogram.map((b) => b.count));

  if (total === 0) {
    out.push({
      level: "info",
      guide: "dataCoverage",
      title: "No R-multiples to read",
      detail: "R needs at least one losing trade to define the unit. Either this period has no losers yet, or no stops were recorded.",
    });
    return out;
  }

  if (f.riskCoverage === 0) {
    out.push({
      level: "info",
      guide: "dataCoverage",
      title: "1R is an estimate, not your actual risk",
      detail: `Every multiple on this tab uses the average loss ($${f.rUnit.toFixed(2)}) as 1R. Set a stop on each position so the distribution is measured against the risk you actually accepted.`,
      metric: `$${f.rUnit.toFixed(2)}/R`,
    });
  }

  if (f.avgR < 0) {
    out.push({
      level: "bad",
      guide: "expectancyR",
      title: "The average trade loses money in R",
      detail: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R per trade. In R terms the book is negative regardless of position size, so this has to be fixed at the setup level.`,
      metric: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R`,
    });
  } else if (f.avgR >= T.rStrong) {
    out.push({
      level: "good",
      guide: "expectancyR",
      title: "Outcomes are genuinely skewed to the right",
      detail: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R per trade. Winners are paying for the losers with room to spare, which is the shape that survives a long sample.`,
      metric: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R`,
    });
  } else {
    out.push({
      level: "warn",
      guide: "expectancyR",
      title: "Average R is positive but thin",
      detail: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R per trade. Small enough that one bad session erases a long stretch — the fix is cutting the losses below -1R, not adding trades.`,
      metric: `${f.avgR.toFixed(2)}R`,
    });
  }

  // "-2R" is the histogram bin for [-2R, -1R) — it is not beyond -2R, so it
  // must not be counted in the left tail. The bins below it are (-3R, -2R) and
  // ≤-3R, which is exactly the "worse than twice the planned risk" set.
  const tailBuckets = ["-3R", "≤-3R"];
  const tail = sum(f.rHistogram.filter((b) => tailBuckets.includes(b.bucket)).map((b) => b.count));
  const tailShare = share(tail, total);
  if (tailShare >= T.leftTailBad * 100) {
    out.push({
      level: "bad",
      guide: "leftTail",
      title: "A chunk of trades close far beyond -1R",
      detail: `${tail} of ${total} trades (${pct(tailShare, 0)}) finish worse than twice the planned risk. Stops are being widened or ignored on exactly the trades that most needed them.`,
      metric: pct(tailShare, 0),
    });
  } else if (tailShare === 0 && f.riskCoverage > 0) {
    out.push({
      level: "good",
      guide: "leftTail",
      title: "No trade exceeded -2R",
      detail: "Every loss respected its planned risk. That is the single cheapest form of risk control and it is holding.",
      metric: "0 trades",
    });
  }

  const positive = f.rHistogram.filter((b) => b.positive);
  const positiveTotal = sum(positive.map((b) => b.count));
  if (positiveTotal >= 5) {
    const early = positive.filter((b) => b.bucket === "+1R").reduce((s, b) => s + b.count, 0);
    const earlyShare = share(early, positiveTotal);
    if (earlyShare >= T.earlyExitWarn) {
      out.push({
        level: "warn",
        guide: "earlyExit",
        title: "Winners are being closed before they run",
        detail: `${pct(earlyShare, 0)} of R-winners finish at +1R and almost nothing reaches +2R. Cutting winners early is the most common way a positive win rate still loses money — check whether targets or patience is the constraint.`,
        metric: pct(earlyShare, 0),
      });
    }
  }

  const scratch = f.rHistogram.find((b) => b.bucket === "+0R")?.count ?? 0;
  const scratchShare = share(scratch, total);
  if (scratchShare >= T.scratchWarn * 100) {
    out.push({
      level: "info",
      guide: "scratchShare",
      title: `${pct(scratchShare, 0)} of trades end around 0R`,
      detail: "Scratches are noise in the distribution. If they share a feature — the same session, the same setup, the same hesitation — filtering them out is a free expectancy gain.",
      metric: pct(scratchShare, 0),
    });
  }

  const lossBucketCount = f.rHistogram.filter((b) => !b.positive).reduce((s, b) => s + b.count, 0);
  const winBucketCount = positiveTotal;
  if (lossBucketCount > 0 && winBucketCount > 0) {
    const winRateFromR = (winBucketCount / (winBucketCount + lossBucketCount)) * 100;
    out.push({
      level: "info",
      guide: "rWinShare",
      title: `${pct(winRateFromR, 0)} of trades close at +1R or better`,
      detail: `${winBucketCount} trades closed at +1R or better and ${lossBucketCount} did not. Compare against the break-even rate the payoff on this tab implies — a lower rate is fine when the payoff is high, and not fine when it is not.`,
      metric: pct(winRateFromR, 0),
    });
  }

  return out;
}

I ran the app on your local server and walked every top-level page, all seven analytics tabs, the Calendar → trade → journal flow, both themes, and widths from 1440 down to 760 px. No code was changed; the only side effect is that I toggled Light and back to Dark while testing.

## Overall read

The visual language is coherent and the core screens are strong: consistent card/border tokens, clear profit/loss colouring, a genuinely useful recommendations layer, a good calendar, and a well-designed report builder. The weak points are not aesthetics — they are **orientation** (where am I, what period am I looking at), **continuity** (losing context in multi-step flows), and **theme/accessibility debt** in the shared components. The biggest wins are small, systemic changes rather than redesigns.

## P0 — things that actively get in the way

**1. Light theme is visibly broken.** In light mode the Import page's headline "Drop your CSV here" is `#f0f0ff` on white — almost invisible — and the description text and MetaTrader banner wash out. The sidebar wordmark and account name are also nearly invisible. Positive values keep `#00e57a` on white (~1.9:1 contrast). The cause is ~92 hardcoded dark-theme colours across nine UI files, on top of tokens in [globals.css](app/globals.css). Fix this by splitting semantic tokens (`--profit`, `--loss`, `--accent`, `--tooltip-bg`, `--chart-grid`) and replacing literals; swap the logo for light mode. Until that's done, the Light option is a trap — hiding it would be more honest than shipping it half-applied.

**2. Unsaved trade edits disappear silently.** [TradePanel.tsx](app/components/TradePanel.tsx) keeps edits in local state, and the X, the overlay click and Escape all call `onClose` without checking dirty state. A user can change entry price, risk, tags and MAE/MFE, then click outside and lose everything. Add dirty tracking with a confirm, or autosave like the journal editor.

**3. First-run is a dead end.** With no accounts, the Dashboard's only CTA is "Import CSV"; the Import page then says "create one first" but offers no link or button. Inline "Create account" from Import (or a two-button empty state: Create account / Import) closes the loop.

**4. There is no way to find a trade anymore.** After removing the Journal list, the only route to a trade is Calendar → correct month → correct day → trade. If you remember the instrument or ticket rather than the date, you're stuck. A global "Find trade" (symbol, ticket, date) in the header — or a Ctrl/Cmd-K palette — restoring the trade panel is the functionality the Journal list used to provide, without bringing the tab back.

**5. Shortcuts fire behind open surfaces.** The key handler in [page.tsx](app/page.tsx) has no guard for an open trade panel or shortcuts modal, so `D` navigates away while a drawer is open. Esc closes the trade panel but not the Calendar day drawer. Also, `/` is the only way to discover the shortcut list — add a visible "?" affordance.

## P1 — orientation and flow

**6. The Dashboard has no page header.** Calendar, Accounts, Import, Export, Playbook, Prop Firm and Settings all have an h2 + subtitle (+ actions on the right); the Dashboard starts cold with the period filter. A shared `PageHeader` with title, subtitle and actions would make the app feel like one product. Put the period/symbol filter in its action slot, add presets (7d / 30d / MTD / YTD / All), and state the scope in human terms: "Showing 14 of 53 trades · 20–26 Oct" instead of the current "Process, risk and behaviour across every tab".

**7. The journal flow loses its place.** Calendar → day → trade → "Open Full Journal" is four clicks, and "Back to Calendar" remounts the page, dropping the selected day and scroll position. Add next/previous trade in the editor plus a sticky day context, preserve `selectedDay` when returning, and show a small "journal missing" dot on calendar days/trades. This directly replaces what the Journal preview used to give you.

**8. The sample caveat is the hero finding.** Under 30 trades, `buildInsights` prepends the caveat, so [InsightPanel](app/components/AnalyticsCards.tsx) renders "Small sample" as the full hero card with a five-band graded bar — while the actual worst finding becomes a collapsed row. That contradicts "worst finding first" and makes a context notice look like a score. Keep the caveat, but as a compact banner above the panel; promote the worst real finding back to the hero.

**9. Analytics density.** Six KPI cards repeat above every tab, and the tab strip scrolls out of view while reading long tabs. A sticky sub-nav under the header (or below the KPI strip) and a slightly more compact KPI row would cut a lot of scrolling without hiding anything.

**10. Export has three scroll containers** (main + builder + preview) and the primary button says "Export 53 Trades" when it downloads a PDF. Label it "Download PDF" and keep one footer action visible. Also decide the date relationship with the Dashboard: right now the dashboard can be filtered to 14 trades while Export covers all 53, which can produce a report for a different period than the screen behind it.

## P2 — clarity, accessibility, polish

- **Copy fixes:** Calendar says "Days 25W / 28L" but those are *trades* (the real trading-day count is in the card below); "Click any trade to open the journal panel" opens the trade editor; "Symbol" means the *market/underlying* (GER40/US100), not the contract. Date/time formats mix `2026-10-14`, `10/20/2026`, `Oct 16`, `10:07` and `10:07 AM`.
- **Click targets:** calendar cells, trade cards and the import dropzone are `<div onClick>` with no role, focus or keyboard activation. Make them real buttons/links, add focus-visible rings (inputs currently use `outline: none`), `aria-current` on nav, and Esc on the day drawer.
- **Type size:** many labels, chart captions and badges are 10–11 px. Raising the floor to 12–13 px would noticeably improve scanning on a laptop.
- **Responsive:** at 900 and 760 px the three KPI columns stay three wide and wrap headers into two lines; the filter's "Symbol" label detaches from its select. Move to `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))` and collapse or iconify the sidebar below ~1100 px.
- **Cold-load flash:** `loading` exists in context but is never consumed, so the app can flash "No trades yet" and an empty sidebar before the fetch resolves. A skeleton for the shell and Dashboard fixes it.
- **Accounts:** cards show only initial balance and an icon-only delete; it isn't obvious that clicking a card activates the account. Show current equity/P&L, an explicit "Set active", and label the destructive control.
- **Prop Firm:** the Monte Carlo fan is 60 spaghetti paths, which is striking but hard to read. Default to the 5–95% band + median + target, with "Show sampled paths" as a toggle — same information, far lower cognitive load.
- **Import:** the page references `QuantEdgeExport.mq5` and `MQL5\Files` but offers no download or numbered steps. A three-step block ("1 Download exporter → 2 Run on an MT5 chart → 3 Drop the CSV") would make first import self-serve.
- **Settings:** the Dashboard's daily loss / max trades strip reads settings that no screen can set (defaults are 0, so it never appears). Either expose "Daily risk controls" in Settings or remove the strip. "Clear all trades" belongs in a visually distinct Danger Zone, not beside export buttons.

## Suggested order

**Quick wins (about an hour):** Dashboard header + filter presets; dirty-close guard on TradePanel; shortcut/overlay guard + Esc for the day drawer; copy fixes (`Days` → `Trades`, `Export N Trades` → `Download PDF`); loading skeleton; `aria-current`.

**Half-day:** tokenise colours and fix Light mode (or hide it); responsive KPI grids and collapsible sidebar; caveat-as-banner + sticky analytics tabs; journal next/prev + preserved day + missing-journal indicator; Import onboarding and exporter download.

**Deeper:** global trade search; unified period scope between Dashboard and Export; Prop Firm chart simplification; account cards with live equity.

What I would *not* change: the dark-first palette, the calendar grid, the worst-first recommendation model, the report preview, or the single-route navigation. None of the suggestions removes a figure or a screen — they mostly reorganise what is already there.

Progress note:
Applied the quick wins and half-day items from the review. Here’s what changed, how it was verified, and what I deliberately left for a second pass.

## Theme and readability

- Added semantic colour tokens (`--profit`, `--loss`, `--warning`, `--tooltip-bg`, `--chart-grid`, `--calendar-empty`) with light-mode variants in [globals.css](app/globals.css), and replaced the hardcoded dark palette across pages and components with them.
- Light mode now uses darker accent shades via [useSettings.ts](app/hooks/useSettings.ts); the old bright neon green remains the dark-theme accent. The sidebar logo switches to the light asset.
- Fixed a subtle regression the token pass exposed: SVG presentation attributes such as `fill="var(--profit)"` are invalid and render black. A small attribute-to-token map in `globals.css` keeps Recharts series and Lucide icons coloured correctly in both themes. This was caught by inspecting computed styles, not just the code.
- Native controls now follow the app theme through `color-scheme`.

## Navigation and safety

- Dashboard now has the same title + subtitle header as every other page, and the period control gained **7D / 30D / MTD / YTD / All** presets, a clearer **Market** label, and a scope line such as “Showing 14 of 53 trades · 4 trading days · 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-26”.
- Clearing the date range now actually removes the stored range; previously it reappeared on reload.
- Page changes reset the main scroll position.
- Single-letter shortcuts are ignored while the trade panel or shortcuts sheet is open; Escape still dismisses overlays. The sidebar now has a visible keyboard-shortcuts button.
- [TradePanel.tsx](app/components/TradePanel.tsx) tracks unsaved changes: X, overlay click, Escape and “Open Full Journal” warn before discarding.
- Added a shell skeleton so cold loads no longer flash “No trades yet”.

## Journal flow

- The editor has **previous/next trade** controls with position (e.g. 23 / 53) and flushes pending autosave before switching.
- “Back to Calendar” reopens the day you came from instead of remounting at the top of the month.
- Calendar days show an amber dot when trades lack notes; the day drawer labels each trade “No journal entry yet”.
- Fixed an issue found during testing: opening and leaving an unjournalled trade used to write an empty TipTap document, falsely marking it as journalled. The editor now only saves real edits or a deliberate clear. The test row I touched was restored to its original empty state.

## Analytics and copy

- The small-sample caveat is now a compact banner above the panel; the worst actionable finding is the hero again.
- The analytics tab strip is sticky while scrolling.
- Calendar’s misleading “Days” stat is now **Trades**; the day-drawer hint describes opening the trade, not the “journal panel”.
- The PDF button now reads **Download PDF · N trades** instead of “Export N Trades”.
- Metric and chart grids use auto-fit columns, and the sidebar collapses to a 72px icon rail below 1100px with accessible labels and `aria-current`.

import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Search, X, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, CornerDownLeft } from "lucide-react";
import { useApp } from "../context/AppContext";
import { Trade } from "../lib/types";

// TipTap stores the journal as a JSON document. Searching the raw string would
// only ever match structural keys, so flatten the text nodes instead.
function journalText(raw: string | null | undefined): string {
  if (!raw) return "";
  try {
    const doc = JSON.parse(raw);
    if (doc?.type === "doc" && Array.isArray(doc.content)) {
      return doc.content
        .flatMap((node: any) =>
          Array.isArray(node.content)
            ? node.content.filter((n: any) => n.type === "text").map((n: any) => n.text)
            : []
        )
        .join(" ");
    }
  } catch {}
  return raw;
}

function haystack(t: Trade): string {
  return [
    t.symbol,
    t.underlying,
    t.date,
    t.direction,
    t.status,
    t.exitReason,
    Array.isArray(t.tags) ? t.tags.join(" ") : "",
    journalText(t.journalEntry),
  ]
    .join(" ")
    .toLowerCase();
}

const money = (v: number) =>
  `${v < 0 ? "-" : v > 0 ? "+" : ""}$${Math.abs(v).toLocaleString("en-US", { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;

const RESULT_LIMIT = 8;

// listened for here rather than in the single-letter shortcut handler, which
// deliberately ignores modified keys.

  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const close = useCallback(() => {
    setOpen(false);
    setQuery("");
    setActive(0);
  }, []);

  const openSearch = useCallback(() => {
    // The trade drawer owns the screen; stacking a palette over it would put
    // two Escape handlers on the same key.
    if (selectedTrade) return;
    setOpen(true);
  }, [selectedTrade]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && (e.key === "k" || e.key === "K")) {
        e.preventDefault();
        setOpen((prev) => {
          if (prev) return false;
          if (selectedTrade) return prev;
          return true;
        });
        setQuery("");
        setActive(0);
      }
    };
    const onRequest = () => openSearch();
    window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
    window.addEventListener("quantedge:search", onRequest);
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
      window.removeEventListener("quantedge:search", onRequest);
    };

  useEffect(() => {

  const results = useMemo(() => {

    const pool = q

  const choose = (trade: Trade) => {
    close();
    setSelectedTrade(trade);
  };

  const onInputKey = (e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {

      close();
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === "ArrowDown") {

      choose(results[active]);

        }}>

          <input
            ref={inputRef}
            value={query}
            onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
            onKeyDown={onInputKey}
            placeholder="Search symbol, date, tag, setup or journal…"
            aria-label="Search trades"
            style={{
              flex: 1, background: "transparent", border: "none", outline: "none",
              color: "var(--text-primary)", fontSize: "14px",
              fontFamily: "'DM Sans', sans-serif",
            }}
          />
          <button
            onClick={close}
            aria-label="Close search"
            style={{ background: "none", border: "none", cursor: "pointer", color: "var(--text-muted)", padding: "2px", display: "flex" }}
          >
            <X size={15} />
          </button>
        </div>

        <div ref={listRef} style={{ maxHeight: "46vh", overflowY: "auto", padding: "6px" }}>
          {results.length === 0 && (
            <div style={{ padding: "28px 16px", textAlign: "center", fontSize: "13px", color: "var(--text-muted)" }}>
              {query.trim()

                : "No trades in this account yet."}
            </div>
          )}

          {results.map((t, i) => {
            const selected = i === active;
            const tags = Array.isArray(t.tags) ? t.tags : [];
            return (
              <button
                key={t.id}
                onMouseEnter={() => setActive(i)}
                onClick={() => choose(t)}
                style={{
                  width: "100%", display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: "12px",
                  padding: "10px 12px", borderRadius: "9px", border: "none",

            <span style={{ display: "flex", alignItems: "center", gap: "3px" }}><CornerDownLeft size={11} /> open</span>
            <span>esc close</span>
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </>
  );

+    if (doc?.type === "doc" && Array.isArray(doc.content)) {
+      return doc.content
+        .flatMap((node: any) =>
+          Array.isArray(node.content)
+            ? node.content.filter((n: any) => n.type === "text").map((n: any) => n.text)
+            : []
+        )
+        .join(" ");
+    }
+  } catch {}
+  return raw;
+}
